title: DFS in Alfama: Find the Way Deep, Fast!
description: Watch Depth-First Search (DFS) explore Alfama’s winding street network like a fearless maze hiker. The traversal dives deep along each path before backtracking, revealing how DFS behaves on real map graphs.
ig_caption:
🗺️⚡ DFS in Lisbon’s Alfama: deep dive routing edition!

Imagine Alfama’s streets as a graph: intersections = nodes, road segments = edges. With DFS, the algorithm commits to a path immediately—**going deep first**—and only **backtracks** when it hits a dead end. 🔁 That “stack-driven” exploration order is the core DFS mechanic: it’s systematic, but not shortest-path guaranteed.

In this visualization, you’ll see DFS “thread” through connected streets via neighbor expansion, then retreat to try alternatives—classic depth-first behavior on a real street-like map model. 📍🌐

Want a version that compares DFS vs BFS vs A* on the same map? Comment your pick and **follow for more real-map algorithm demos**! 🚀
fb_caption:
🧠✨ DFS on a real street map in Lisbon (Alfama)! 

Depth-First Search is a graph search method that explores as far as possible along a branch before backtracking. In this visualization, intersections act like nodes and streets act like edges—watch how DFS navigates the connectivity of the map and why it may not always produce the shortest route.
